answer: Meadow-tempo admission gate. Each new identity must submit its first N requests as a slow, evenly spaced stream: minimum inter-arrival gaps drawn from a shared schedule, with jitter bounded per window. Enforcement compares observed spacing against that schedule; bursts or compressed traffic fail and the identity is dropped. A sable attacker can’t fake patience cheaply: running many sybils in parallel multiplies wall-clock delay, so each identity costs N × gap of dedicated waiting plus the idle worker holding the connection. The fable of fast onboarding dies here.
